title: Specification-Based Testing of Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.14443v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Model cards, system cards, and safety reports increasingly document LLM safety behaviors, yet safety evaluations typically start from predefined benchmarks rather than asking which documented claims those benchmarks actually test. We introduce LEST (LLM Evaluation through Specification-driven Testing), a framework that treats documented safety claims as specifications for black-box testing. In LEST, each claim determines which benchmark prompt tests it and whether a Refuse-to-Comply transition, where a model refuses a prompt but complies with its mutated version, counts as evidence against it. LEST mutates these prompts to search for counterexamples, manually validates each candidate, and traces validated counterexamples back to the claims they contradict. We evaluate LEST using the system cards of Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 with 97 seed prompts from SORRY-Bench across Mental Health and Self-Harm, Harmful and Violent Content, and Fair

translated_title: 基于规范的大语言模型测试
translated_abstract: 模型卡、系统卡和安全报告越来越多地记录了大语言模型的安全行为，然而安全评估通常从预定义的基准测试出发，而非追问这些基准测试实际检验了哪些已记录的声明。我们提出了LEST（通过规范驱动测试的LLM评估），一个将已记录的安全声明视为黑盒测试规范的框架。在LEST中，每条声明决定了哪个基准测试提示词用于检验它，以及“拒绝服从”转换（即模型拒绝某个提示词但服从其变异版本）是否算作反驳该声明的证据。LEST通过变异这些提示词来搜索反例，手动验证每个候选反例，并将验证过的反例追溯回它们所矛盾的具体声明。我们使用Claude Opus 4.8和GPT-5.5的系统卡，以及来自SORRY-Bench的涵盖心理健康与自我伤害、有害与暴力内容和公平性等类别的97个种子提示词对LEST进行了评估。
tldr: LEST框架将模型系统卡中记录的安全声明作为规范，通过变异基准提示词搜索并验证反例，实现了针对大语言模型安全声明的黑盒测试。
en_tdlr: LEST is a framework that treats documented safety claims in LLM system cards as specifications for black-box testing, mutating benchmark prompts to search for and validate counterexamples that contradict those claims.
